=== UNIT.md
# Asset build enumeration and verifier integration trial

Candidate02 after actual review01; new bytes pending delta review. This provides the build-side real filesystem enumeration missing from the accepted asset verifier unit. It does not build the actual browser report, publish a release, compile a product HostAssetPin or select a production build channel. fixtures/release/report contains three explicitly labelled synthetic files, used only to test interoperability.

The pure build helper takes a retained trusted asset-root directory descriptor, an exact explicit release-relative role map, supported projection schema digests and the build channel. It visits every directory entry, refuses any symlink/nonregular entry without following it, streams each regular file through SHA256, and returns the exact canonical private manifest bytes plus private HostAssetPinV1 data. A prior manifest is excluded only by exact path; a directory or symlink at that path refuses. An unlisted regular file, missing declared member, unknown role or undeclared manifest alias refuses. No extension/hidden-file filter silently omits files. The helper does not write the tree or read a package manager/network. Caller build custody supplies the root handle and admits schema digests; the returned pin record is build data, never a file the runtime may treat as authority.

The selected trial build namespace is lowercase ASCII path segments, starts with a letter/digit, then letters/digits/dot/underscore/hyphen, no trailing dot, at most 255 bytes per segment, 4096 for a release-relative path and 16 path segments. This narrower private output namespace eliminates casefold and Unicode normalization aliases without changing the public LogicalPath or generic verifier grammar. All paths, including directories and the sole manifest, obey it. The manifest is a direct member of the chosen asset root for this build profile. Future asset pipelines needing other names must explicitly revise the profile, not silently normalize filenames. Roles are supplied explicitly, not inferred from extensions.

Trial build caps are 16 supported projection digests, 4096 files, 4096 directories, 16 MiB per member, 4 MiB manifest and 32 MiB aggregate member-plus-manifest bytes. These are root-selected build limits pending review and actual browser bundle measurement, not runtime/performance qualification. Reads are streamed and size-bounded; JSON manifest allocation and directory listing happen before their final size/count checks, under a quiescent trusted build tree. This is not a malicious filesystem resource sandbox. Oversized build inputs fail before returning a pin, never truncate. The runtime must still enforce its accepted 4 MiB manifest profile and exact compiled member sizes. The observed sample is 648 manifest bytes + 151 member bytes, which is fixture sizing only.

File/parent inode comparisons and before/after size/mtime/ctime detect observed replacement or writes. They are not an atomic snapshot or proof against malicious same-process/concurrent writers. Actual build custody must quiesce or retain the selected immutable inputs and publish the manifest/assets together; load-time independent digest verification remains required. Empty directories are permitted because the private manifest inventories regular file bytes; release assembly separately owns directory/delivery nodes.

Eleven Python groups exercise exact inventory/pin/schema construction, genuine regular files, zero-byte notices, manifest self-exclusion and exact backup distinction, missing/extra/hidden/case/Unicode paths, symlinks at manifest/member/directory positions, FIFO/socket/manifest-directory refusal, retained-root path replacement, member/manifest/total boundaries, role/digest/path admission, interrupted reads, growing/same-length changed files and changed directory contents. Small patched test-only limits check exact boundaries; they are not product configuration. build_fixture.py validates both generated private records against the copied owner schemas and explicitly writes only its synthetic fixture artifacts.

An isolated Rust consumer uses unchanged copies of the accepted verifier/platform/identity source, its own locked offline Cargo build, and an independently emitted fixture digest constant. The emitted manifest loads through the actual retained-directory adapter and accepted byte verifier. The test selects every entry of a three-schema compatibility list, including the middle one, and asserts the retained digest, complete member paths/roles/bytes and raw manifest identity. This closes the accepted unit's projection-accessor regression gap for integration without changing its frozen bytes. Cargo Clippy -D warnings and fmt --check pass. No product reporting-to-platform edge is added; this consumer is an isolated interoperability test.

Run the reference Python -I -B tests/test_report_asset_manifest.py; explicitly run build_fixture.py in the trusted reference env; then cargo test/clippy --locked --offline --manifest-path consumer/Cargo.toml. Ordinary product Cargo builds will not invoke this Python fixture generator. source-pins.json records the unchanged verifier and private owner inputs; root-validation.json records observed commands/tool pins. Complete source/bootstrap/tool closure, inventory/tool selection, actual offline bundle+licenses, immutable publication, private compiled pin/sole build channel, compiled projection digest join, D9 host delivery, Linux/platform and release inventory qualifications remain required. Neither these tests nor the labelled fixture are the actual OpenSIP report.

Candidate02 adds seven permanent groups derived from the actual reviewer probes, plus their two real filesystem bundles. The Rust integration test checks all 19 projection/bundle pairs (3 nested, 16 deeply nested). Tests preserve the real traversal-order counterexample, descriptor flags, replacement, bounds, manifest exclusion, role and namespace checks. test-origins.json pins the original reviewer sources and describes adaptations. A controlled early-EOF test with unchanged metadata exercises the final byte-count check. OSError now becomes a typed ASSET_FILESYSTEM refusal; no raw OS text is a public report. The assembler checks aggregate member bytes before reading a member that would exceed the bound. Windows device basenames, including extensions, are refused in this private namespace.

To reproduce the extra Rust integration test, first run tests/review_regressions.py with TOOL OWNER_JSON PRIVATE_INTEROP_DIR RESULT_JSON, then set ASSEMBLY_INTEROP_DIR to that fixture directory for Cargo test and Clippy. Use a short absolute scratch path because the deliberate 16-segment fixture approaches the platform pathname limit. The probe itself uses descriptor-relative operations. Ordinary product builds will not run these trial fixture generators. The unit socket test uses a retained temporary-directory descriptor so long TMPDIR values do not exceed AF_UNIX pathname limits. Seven adopted probe groups and two Rust groups pass; source-pins.json still verifies all 14 unchanged owner/verifier input copies.
